questions.statement: It is white. It comes from cows. Many children drink it for breakfast. What is it?
questions.context: En muchas casas de Bogotá el desayuno incluye una bebida blanca que viene de la vaca.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Soda' is a sweet fizzy drink from a bottle or can, and it does not come from cows.
Incorrect. 'Coffee' is a brown drink made from coffee beans, not a white drink from cows.
Incorrect. 'Orange juice' is orange and comes from fruit, not from cows.
Correct. 'Milk' is the white drink that comes from cows.

questions.explanation:
La palabra 'milk' significa leche. Las pistas son el color blanco y el origen: viene de la vaca. 'Soda', 'coffee' y 'orange juice' también son bebidas, pero ninguna es blanca ni sale de la vaca.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "Sofía makes a sandwich with two slices of ___."
questions.context: Sofía prepara las onces para el colegio en su casa de Pereira.

options.feedback: Correct. A sandwich is made with two slices of 'bread'.
Incorrect. 'Water' is a drink; you cannot make slices of water.
Incorrect. 'Juice' is a drink, so it cannot be cut into slices for a sandwich.
Incorrect. 'Rice' is small grains; it does not come in slices.

questions.explanation:
'Bread' es pan. Un sándwich se hace con dos tajadas ('slices') de pan. Las otras opciones son bebidas o granos, y ninguna se puede cortar en tajadas para armar un sándwich.

questions.statement: It has no color and no taste. You drink it every day. What is it?
questions.context: En la clase de ciencias de un colegio de Cali hablan de la bebida más importante para el cuerpo.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Milk' is white, so it has a color.
Incorrect. 'Juice' has the color and the taste of the fruit.
Incorrect. 'Hot chocolate' is brown and sweet, so it has color and taste.
Correct. 'Water' has no color and no taste, and we drink it every day.

questions.explanation:
'Water' es agua. Es la única de estas bebidas sin color y sin sabor. La leche es blanca, el jugo sabe a fruta y el chocolate caliente es café y dulce.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "In Colombia, many people eat ___ and beans for lunch."
questions.context: En Colombia muchas familias almuerzan arroz con fríjoles.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Rice and beans' is a common lunch, and 'rice' is a food you eat.
Incorrect. 'Juice' is a drink; you drink it, you do not 'eat' it.
Incorrect. 'Milk' is a drink, so it does not go with the verb 'eat'.
Incorrect. 'Tea' is a hot drink, not a food you eat with beans.

questions.explanation:
'Rice' es arroz. El verbo 'eat' (comer) pide una comida, no una bebida. Por eso solo 'rice' completa bien la oración: 'eat rice and beans'.

questions.statement:
Read the dialogue.
Waiter: "What would you like to drink?"
Boy: "___"
questions.context: En un restaurante de Manizales, el mesero le pregunta a un niño qué quiere tomar.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Chicken' is food, but the waiter asks about a drink.

options.text: A glass of orange juice, please.
options.feedback: Correct. The waiter asks about a drink, and 'a glass of orange juice' is a drink.
Incorrect. This answers 'How old are you?', not a question about drinks.
Incorrect. The question asks 'what', so 'yes' does not answer it, and 'hungry' is about food.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta 'What would you like to drink?' significa '¿qué te gustaría tomar?'. La respuesta debe nombrar una bebida, como 'a glass of orange juice' (un vaso de jugo de naranja).

questions.statement:
Read: "Tomás has breakfast at 6:30. He eats eggs and bread, and he drinks hot chocolate."
What does Tomás drink?
questions.context: Tomás vive en Tunja y desayuna temprano antes de ir al colegio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text does not mention milk.
Incorrect. The text does not say that Tomás drinks water.
Incorrect. Orange juice is not in the text.
Correct. The text says 'he drinks hot chocolate'.

questions.explanation:
La respuesta está en la frase 'he drinks hot chocolate' (él toma chocolate caliente). 'Eggs and bread' son lo que come, y las otras bebidas no aparecen en el texto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: La profesora de un colegio de Cúcuta pide clasificar palabras de comida y bebida.

options.feedback: Correct. Water, milk and juice are all drinks.
Incorrect. 'Rice' and 'bread' are foods; only 'milk' is a drink.
Incorrect. 'Chicken' is a food, so this group is not only drinks.
Incorrect. 'Eggs' are food and 'soup' is eaten with a spoon; only 'water' is a drink.

questions.explanation:
Para elegir hay que revisar cada palabra del grupo. 'Water' (agua), 'milk' (leche) y 'juice' (jugo) son bebidas. En los otros grupos aparecen comidas como 'rice', 'bread', 'chicken' o 'eggs'.

questions.statement:
Read the school menu: "Lunch: chicken, rice and salad. Drink: lemonade. Dessert: mango."
Luis says: "There is no drink on the menu." Is he right?
questions.context: Luis lee el menú del almuerzo escolar en un colegio de Barranquilla.

options.text: Yes, because mango is a drink.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Mango' is a fruit, and the menu lists it as the dessert.

options.text: Yes, because there is only food.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The menu has a line called 'Drink'.

options.text: No, because the drink is lemonade.
options.feedback: Correct. The menu says 'Drink: lemonade', so Luis is wrong.

options.text: No, because the drink is rice.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Rice' is part of the lunch, not the drink.

questions.explanation: El menú tiene una línea 'Drink: lemonade' (bebida: limonada), así que Luis se equivoca. Hay que leer cada parte: 'Lunch' es el plato, 'Drink' la bebida y 'Dessert' el postre.
